newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt must avoid future bickering-economist.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt must avoid future bickering-economist.

text.p: The warm welcome given by investors to the Thai baht's managed float last week won't help the country's economy if members of its coalition government continue bickering, a senior economist said on Monday.

Warapatr Todhanakasem, executive chairman of SITCA Investment and Securities Plc, said the Thai investment climate would suffer if the coalition partners in the government of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh did not agree on policies.
"As long as the coalition government is weakened by internal bickering, it would be tough for the economy to recover," Warapatr said.
Chavalit's former finance minister Amnuay Viravan quit in June after disagreements over tax policy with Industry Minister Korn Dabbaransi.
He was replaced by Thanong Bidaya, who became the country's sixth finance minister since 1995 under three administrations.
"Foreigners will switch investment elsewhere and this will shatter the government's hopes," Warapatr told reporters.
Thailand last Wednesday abandoned its long-standing practice of fixing the baht against a dollar-dominated basket of currencies in favour of a new managed float system.
Thai shares rose around 25 percent in value during three trading sessions after the float before slipping on profit-taking on Monday.
"We must not jump to conclusions now that foreign investment has returned following sharp gains of the stock market last week due to foreign buying. We're overreacting," Warapatr said.

He said the government must take further steps to boost the Thai economy as soon as possible if it did not want the baht, attacked repeatedly by investors before its float, to come under speculative pressure once again.
"The Thai economy isn't too bad now. The government must have strict monetary and financial discipline if it wants to see the economy survive," Warapatr said.
